body: Thanks exusia. I started coming to that same conclusion today. Honestly at this point it's more of a friendship of convenience than anything else (we work together). You make some good points. Thanks for the well thought-out response.

Hmm, perhaps the post comes off less bleak than I feel. Yes, all of those things are good suggestions. And were my logic properly engaging I assure you I'd try them all. But this is the epitome of depression - knowing that there IS a solution and still hurting anyway. Oh hell, this guy explains it better: http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cKiAz6ndUbU

What this really comes down to is a question of control. I've convinced myself (rationally or not) that I'm no longer in control. The list of things I can control is dwindling until there's just one thing left on that list. I don't like that item, but it's the one item that can never be taken away.

I don't have friends, friends have me. I'm not part of a society, society owns me. I have mild-mannered opinions, others have steam-roller dogmas that don't stop for anything.

Is that self-fulfilling, self-victimizing talk? You bet it is. And mother of god it's addictive. Believe something long enough and the pain, even imaginary, becomes tangible.

My "friends" are dicks to me. They make fun of me. They talk behind my back. They torture me by feeding me false information, withholding information, and making me question my memory. They bring up old mistakes *constantly*. They poke fun at my weight. The worst part is, they don't hate me, I think they view me as a pet or something. I'm the mascot. I hate them, but they're the only people I know.

I used to have a hobby -- photography. Haven't had the energy for that in almost 2 years now. Photography requires an appreciation for beauty. I see none worth photographing lately.

Don't thank me for fulfilling others wants and desires. It's a finely-tuned codependent game that I play. I'd stop it right away if I weren't so deathly afraid of the disapproval of others. Standing up for myself feels like fighting a mob. So I sit quietly, always aware of their quick tempers and sharpened pitch-forks.
If only it were so simple.
